t: Delphi was a small city-state in Phocis that existed to run the sanctuary of Apollo and the most famous oracle of the Greek world.
The Amphictyonic League of twelve peoples protected the shrine, ran the Pythian Games and could proclaim sacred wars.
Phocians, Macedonians, Aetolians and finally Romans controlled it in turn, until Greece came under Roman oversight in 146 BCE.
dyk: Greeks believed Delphi was the centre of the earth: Zeus released two eagles from opposite ends of the world and they met there, a spot marked by a stone navel, the omphalos.
ev: First Sacred War: the Amphictyons destroy Kirrha and consecrate its plain to Apollo
The Pythian Games are reorganised as a panhellenic festival
The temple of Apollo burns and is rebuilt with contributions from across Greece
The Greeks dedicate the Serpent Column after the victory at Plataea
Third Sacred War: the Phocians seize Delphi and spend its treasures
A Gallic army under Brennus is driven back from Delphi
Rome ends Aetolian control and restores Delphian autonomy
